setlist.title: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews): A long, gradual lead-in from Drums built to Phil's thundering bass blast opening the song; The Other One into Stella Blue was called a great highlight [10][11]
- **Stella Blue** (2 reviews): Stella Blue reached a sweet peak; Named as a highlight [19][20]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jack Straw was a sweet, tight opener [15]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet into Fire was singled out as a blazing highlight [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Jam without Jerry**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-08-16.sbd.unknown.32019.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 156 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says much better recordings exist and recommends the Charlie Miller upgrade instead of this soundboard; Reviewer calls this soundboard the best-sounding possible, with no better soundboard existing; The sound is disrupted during Jerry's solo [1][14][16]
- **gd1981-08-16.148439.sbd.clugston.remaster32019.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 158 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1981-08-16.135517.nak300.schley.flac1644**: audience recording; 21 songs; 153 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Small cuts at the starts of Loser, Minglewood and Rooster [3]
- **gd1981-08-16.153277.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 156 min [4]
- **gd1981-08-16.nak300.miller.94900.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 152 min; rated 3.57/5 by 7 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer found the sound nice [19]

## Around the show

- The hall was so hot the listener sweated from arrival to departure [9]
- Ken Kesey, Ken Babbs and the Thunder Machine joined the band and were a standout [9]
- Years later Phil told the listener he also loved playing that bass part [10]
- Hitchhiked from Portland; spare tickets went for $5 outside; the gym-like arena was only about two-thirds full [11]
- After set one, crowds of hippies drummed on overturned garbage cans in the restroom area [13]
- After the show, a stranger handed the listener some cocaine [13]
- Listener had a backstage pass, sat in the bleachers with Kesey and Walton during set one [17]
- At the break, food and drink were served in a wrestling locker room downstairs [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-08-16.sbd.unknown.32019.flac16**: source: SBD > ? > (Cx?) > CDR [1]. Also: The soundboard lacked the first two songs; the uploader added them from an audience tape, pitch-corrected and volume-matched in Soundforge [1]
- **gd1981-08-16.148439.sbd.clugston.remaster32019.flac16**: source: Remaster by Scott Clugston [2]. Also: Remaster of the 32019 soundboard with fresh patches, including in El Paso, Peggy O and Little Red Rooster; Jim Vita's and Charlie Miller's Nakamichi 300 source supplies Jack Straw, Friend Of The Devil, the El Paso transition and several patches [2]
- **gd1981-08-16.135517.nak300.schley.flac1644**: taped by Brian Schley; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > lead Sony D5 > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's, FOB recording by Brian Schley. [3]. Also: Schley's Nakamichi 300 master; the first set of the 9381/94900 source copies it, while set two came from a different deck [3]
- **gd1981-08-16.153277.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 capsules > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell UDXLII-S) [4]. Also: Brian Schley's Nakamichi 300 source supplies patches in Drums and the Drums to Space transition [4]
- **gd1981-08-16.nak300.miller.94900.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Nakamichi 300 -> Master Cassette -> Dat -> CD -> SHN [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1981-08-16 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1981-08-16-backstage-pass/) [22]
